annotationRationale: The integer restriction reduces the factored difference of squares to two positive factor pairs. The principal square root determines the allowed sign of m.
sourceMethod: Follows the official factor-pair solution, first taking n positive and then restoring its negative values. Explains positivity of the factors and why the factor list is exhaustive.

review.mathCheck: Independently, \(m\ge0\) and \(|n|\ge7\). For positive \(n\), the ordered factor pairs of 49 give \((m,n)=(0,7),(24,25)\). Restoring negative \(n\) gives exactly four solutions, choice D; the zero endpoint is included.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of MAA Q11 on page 5: principal-root sign, difference-of-squares factorization, positive factor pairs, then sign symmetry.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed integer-equation and factorization skills match the method. Principal-root conventions and finding factors are appropriate supporting knowledge.
